title: Djisktra's Algorithm
problemStatement: Single-source shortest paths on a graph with non-negative edge weights.
intuition: Greedily settle the closest unsettled node (like BFS, but priority queue replaces FIFO). Fails with negative edges — use Bellman-Ford there.

approaches.title: Brute: Bellman-Ford style relax-all (works but slower)
approaches.idea: Relax every edge |V|-1 times — handles negatives too, but O(nm).
limitations: Correct for non-negative too, but too slow when Dijkstra applies

approaches.title: Optimal: Dijkstra with min-heap
approaches.idea: dist[], heap of (d,u); skip stale entries.
approaches.time: O((n + m) log n) with binary heap
approaches.dryRun: Settle nodes in increasing distance order; once popped with dist[u], it is final (non-negative weights).
approaches.whyWorks: Non-negative weights ⇒ no future path can improve a settled node.
limitations: Negative edge → WRONG — algorithm assumption violated

specialTechnique.title: Algorithm choice table
specialTechnique.body:
Unweighted → BFS
Non-negative weights → Dijkstra
Negative edges → Bellman-Ford
0/1 weights → 0-1 BFS
All-pairs → Floyd-Warshall (dense) / Dijkstra from each (sparse)

followUps: K shortest paths / constraints on stops?
interviewInsight: Draw the comparison table on the board before coding — that habit separates strong interview answers.
